response.rationale: The co-occurrence of a catecholamine-secreting pheochromocytoma and a calcitonin/CEA-secreting medullary thyroid carcinoma with calcified thyroid nodules defines MEN2; isolated pheochromocytoma or isolated medullary thyroid carcinoma explains only one component of the syndrome. Absent family history does not exclude de novo MEN2.

rejected.why: Accounts for the calcitonin/CEA elevation and thyroid nodules, but not for the massive urinary metanephrines; represents a component of the syndrome rather than the unifying diagnosis.

Explains the adrenergic symptoms and elevated metanephrines, but not the markedly elevated calcitonin, elevated CEA, calcified thyroid nodules, or elevated PTH; therefore also only a component of the full picture.
